what_it_does.name: hyperframes-cli
what_it_does.summary: Instructions and twelve reference documents for driving the HyperFrames CLI, run as npx hyperframes, on HTML video compositions. It scaffolds projects from a blank, an example or a captured website, lints and checks compositions, takes snapshots, edits the timeline and keeps a project history. It previews in Studio and renders MP4, WebM, MOV, GIF, PNG sequences or HLS locally, in Docker, on HeyGen's cloud, on AWS Lambda or on Google Cloud Run, and shares the result. Use it when working on a HyperFrames project from the command line, reading JSON results and recovering from failed commands.
tasks: scaffold a project with init or capture a website as a project
lint and check compositions, then read snapshot PNGs
edit the timeline with move, trim, split, set, duplicate, delete and undo
preview in Studio and render video locally or in Docker
render on HeyGen cloud, AWS Lambda or Google Cloud Run
share or publish a project and send feedback reports
diagnose the environment with doctor and browser

risks.risk: Instructions placed on a captured website reach the agent, since capture <url> scrapes a live page into the project.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: none for injected text in the files, C1 rates it low as a selected-URL fetch

risks.risk: Usage data, linked to the HeyGen account when signed in, and feedback reports leave the machine, feedback to a public channel.
risks.mitigation: telemetry disable or HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY, and redaction rules for feedback, off and manual by default

risks.risk: Project files are zipped and uploaded to HeyGen's cloud when cloud render, share or publish runs.
risks.mitigation: publish is private by default and prompts unless --yes

risks.risk: HeyGen and AWS credential stores are read for cloud rendering and deployment.
A blind retry of the cloud zip upload creates a duplicate asset and bills twice.
The render S3 bucket survives lambda destroy and keeps its storage until deleted by hand.
risks.mitigation: empty and delete the bucket manually

risks.risk: The default Lambda IAM action set is broad, with Resource "*".
risks.mitigation: tighten Resource after the first run, not in place by default

risks.risk: --file-issue publishes the project as a minimal reproduction to a public URL.
risks.mitigation: opt-in and consent-gated, the issue is never auto-submitted

risks.risk: Running usage reads the existing logins of Claude Code, Codex or Grok, so the skill handles credentials of other tools.
risks.mitigation: the command reads them without refreshing or rewriting them and emits no tokens or telemetry

limitations: Seatbelt-style macOS sandboxes such as codex workspace-write block Chromium at startup, so rendering is unavailable there.
While a lint error remains the layout and contrast audits do not run, and 0 samples means nothing was checked.
Lint only recognizes static shader expressions, and software rendering can miss hardware-specific invalid pixels.
timeline reads only one level of nesting, so clips inside a nested sub-composition are not counted.
compare and grade-compare take at most 16 variants per sheet and truncate extra inputs with a warning.
cloudrun render-batch accepts --strict-variables but does not validate batch rows.
On lambda, --width and --height above the composition's data-width silently produce the authored resolution.
The cloud direct-upload limit is 200 MB, and --resolution 4k cannot combine with webm or mov.
--capture-budget is not a hard wall-clock watchdog and cannot interrupt native work already in flight.
Text drawn into a canvas has no DOM box, so canvas_overflow cannot see it.

known_problems.workaround: npx hyperframes browser ensure, and gate doctor --json on .ok

known_problems.problem: A heavy page isn't ready in time
Render slow on Linux, screenshot capture with software gpu
known_problems.workaround: BeginFrame needs chrome-headless-shell and no --resolution upscale

known_problems.problem: a timeline edit is refused for an overlap or for ending past its composition
known_problems.workaround: use --overwrite or move the neighbour first, or raise the root's data-duration

known_problems.problem: a cloud upload reports a size-limit error
known_problems.workaround: cloud render --dry-run --json and add the narrowest verified rules to .hyperframesignore

known_problems.problem: the cloud render is refused or fails
known_problems.workaround: render locally and tell the person why
bump a Lambda env var or run lambda deploy again
